name: Sound It Out
tagline: Any sentence they love, built up from its sounds — in your own voice.
description:
Made for one boy with Down syndrome learning to read, and shared for every family like his. Sound It Out makes calm, looping videos for a TV or tablet from one list: anything you add — a name, a word, a whole sentence. Every word is built up from its sounds, each letter lighting up as its sound plays, the gaps shrinking until the sounds become the word; sentences grow word by word and end with your own read of the line, the highlight following your voice.

Colour means exactly one thing on screen: whatever is being said right now. No cartoons, no rewards, no distractions — just words, sounds, and repetition, which is how it sticks.

Starter packs follow the reading research for Down syndrome — personally meaningful words first, then letter sounds, then sounding out, then sentences. Paw Patrol lines a fan actually wants read ("Chase is on the case."), VeggieTales, lines of faith, the lines of an ordinary day, and the skills: letter sounds in phonics order, made-up sounding-out practice words that cannot be memorised as shapes, letter teams, first decodable sentences. A pack is just entries on your list; remove any you like. Words the letter rules would say wrong — "the", "said", "one" — are shown and spoken whole, because a wrong buildup teaches worse than none; magic-e words build the way phonics has taught them for a century, c + ase. And the list of whole-read words is yours to grow: type your own sight words into the Sound Bank, and they are not broken into sounds — not when recording, not in the video.

The voice is the heart of it. Each entry records in a short walk-through — its words, then the whole line — checked as you speak: an "uh" on the end of a consonant, the classic mistake that teaches the wrong sound, is caught on the spot. Words go into a shared bank, so every sentence you add gets cheaper to record than the one before. Everything you record stays on your device, inside your own copy of the app — not in the copy anyone else downloads. Until you record, a real human starter voice covers the 42 letter sounds and a built-in voice covers the packs; an optional speaking voice (GifOS Settings) reads words nobody recorded. Isolated sounds are not sent out.

Tick what to include, pick a look and a thinking-gap, and the app tells you how long the video will run. Play it straight on the screen, or save it as a video file for a USB stick.

Invite family and it behaves like family: anyone who opens the invite link sees the list live, hears the recordings, and can play the video at their house — and can add a sentence of their own for the child. Recording stays with the owner: the microphone follows the person, not the link. A little badge shows who is here.
